headline: Exploited flaws in four products, plus critical NGINX and Java bugs, need patching now
plain_summary: CISA added four flaws to its exploited list, with a November 21 deadline for three. Critical flaws in NGINX, Java and Drupal have fixes, and Apache says a flaw in Roller is being exploited. A Microsoft Python package was published with a credential stealer. The European Commission is dealing with an attack whose cause is not yet known.

items.title: CISA adds four exploited flaws: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Axis, REDCap
items.why: Federal deadline is November 21 for three of them; exploitation is reported, including ransomware on Synology NAS.
items.action: Find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist. Axis 1.x is end of life with no fix (migrate or apply the July 12, 2026 commit); keep Axis, LiteLLM and REDCap off the open internet until addressed.

items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 flaws allow unauthenticated code execution
items.why: CERT-FR says a public proof of concept exists for one of the two flaws.
items.action: Check every NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928, or disable HTTP/2 until patched (remove http2 from the listen line, or set http2 off on 1.25.0 and earlier). Review exposed servers for signs of compromise.

items.title: CISA urges immediate patching of Java flaw 'Java4Shell'
items.why: Java runs inside many third-party apps and appliances, and GreyNoise saw matching requests, with no successful intrusions on its sensors.
items.action: Find every Java runtime, including ones bundled in third-party apps, containers and appliances. Apply Oracle and vendor patches, internet-facing systems first. Until patched, validate and size-limit Base64 input and restrict unauthenticated access. Siemens Industrial Edge Management users: block direct internet access to IEM Pro and Virtual until Siemens releases a fix.

items.title: Apache says Roller code-execution flaw is exploited
items.why: Apache itself reports exploitation of an unauthenticated flaw in versions 4.0.0 to 6.1.4.
items.action: Upgrade Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later. If you cannot, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc mapping and restart; switching off XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.

items.title: Drupal fixes critical flaw that can let attackers reinstall a site
items.why: Drupal says a proof of concept exists and fixed releases are out.
items.action: Update Drupal core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13 (or later). If you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes. Sites on 11.2.x and 10.5.x or older are end of life.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI releases carried a credential stealer
items.why: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 are confirmed malicious and run when Python starts; PyPI has quarantined them.
items.action: Check for Agent Framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 in environments and CI builds, pin to 1.26.0, and rotate Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face and OpenAI credentials and OIDC tokens on any host that installed them.

items.title: About 40 Irish credit unions hit by supplier breach
items.why: Saved payee records were exposed, and credit unions were told only on November 17.
items.action: Credit union members should watch for payment fraud and phishing that uses saved payee details. Credit unions should confirm what Wellington IT holds for them and ask it for access logs.

items.title: European Commission reports attack on staff HR and health systems
items.why: Press reports say HR and insurance systems were down for days; the attacker and any data theft are not yet established.
items.action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.
